replies.author: Equal_Passenger9791
replies.body:
Same prompt isn't always a good comparison, this is particularly true if you've been working intensely with one model, getting familiar with it's quirks in interpretation to reach a particular and refine look, and then just transplant the same prompt into the other model.

Even basic prompts can give very misleading results if you shove them into models where the system prompt is a mystery because one model might have "give the user what they ask for" and the other can say "always assume the user wants a more refined and aesthetic outcome than how they phrase the request", which can result in significant outcome differences for literally the same model.

comments.author: hblok
comments.body:
I have the same experience with ChatGpt vs Claude.

Claude will put in a lot more effort to make a polished holistic solution, and will also add small details (like the clouds, trees and waterline seen in the OP's video) on its own initiative.

I've tried something similar with other games like Pacman and Doom. For monster in Doom, it came up with some hilarious monsters.
